audience: From Class 10 foundations through undergraduate and graduate mathematics, PhD preparation and selected research topics relevant to quantum science.

stages.name: Foundations
stages.subjects: Arithmetic, fractions, powers, equations, sets, logic and proof
stages.question: What do the symbols mean? Which steps are valid?

stages.name: Relationships and shape
stages.subjects: Functions, graphs, coordinate geometry, trigonometry and complex numbers
stages.question: How are quantities related? How do we describe location, angle and rotation?

stages.name: Many quantities together
stages.subjects: Vectors, matrices, linear systems and linear transformations
stages.question: How can we represent and transform several linked quantities at once?

stages.name: Change and accumulation
stages.subjects: Limits, derivatives, integrals and multivariable calculus
stages.question: How fast does something change? What accumulates over time or space?

stages.name: Uncertainty and evidence
stages.subjects: Counting, probability, statistics and stochastic processes
stages.question: What outcomes are possible? What does data support, and with what uncertainty?

stages.name: Evolving systems and computation
stages.subjects: Differential equations, Fourier analysis, numerical methods and optimization
stages.question: How does a system evolve? What frequencies are present? How can we compute or approximate a solution?

stages.name: Structure and connection
stages.subjects: Number theory, abstract algebra, discrete mathematics, graph theory and symmetry
stages.question: Which patterns persist? How do operations and networks fit together?

stages.name: Deeper mathematical frameworks
stages.subjects: Real and complex analysis, measure theory, topology, differential geometry, tensors, Hilbert spaces and operators
stages.question: When do our methods work? How do we reason about more general spaces and transformations?

stages.name: Quantum mathematics and research preparation
stages.subjects: Quantum information mathematics, operator methods, quantum algorithms, error correction and selected research-level connections
stages.question: How does the mathematics come together in quantum theory? Can we read current research, check its assumptions and investigate a claim responsibly?

domains.name: Multilinear algebra, tensors and tensor networks
Hilbert spaces, operators and spectral theory
Quantum algorithms, codes and mathematical quantum theory

language_note: English only for now (founder decision, 6 November 2026). Hindi may follow later as separately reviewed versions.

tiers.T1: Foundation: check the idea and the basic skills
tiers.T5: University: undergraduate exam and textbook-hard problems
tiers.R: Research note: what is open, with verified sources

depth_standard: Every topic chapter climbs from the first missing prerequisite to the ceiling of its topic: the hardest problems that topic produces, up to PhD qualifying level where the topic reaches that far.
Every chapter has a toolkit: each standard technique for the topic, when to use it, why it works, and a worked example.
Every chapter has a problem ladder through every tier from T1 up to its ceiling, at least 5 problems per tier, each with a full solution, the key idea named and the common wrong approaches.
Every theorem used is proved in the chapter or linked to the chapter where it is proved; graduate results carry complete hypotheses.
Every chapter ends with a mastery check: a mixed set across all its tiers. A learner who can solve it has mastered the topic.
Past exam problems are used only with a verified source (exam, year, paper, question number). All other problems are original. No invented attributions.
Chapter 0 is an orientation chapter and is exempt from the problem ladder.
